From a team at EBP[^transp] comes an [interesting deep(ish) dive][post] into a 
"talk to the map" solution – that is, a chatbot in a map interface. The article 
(in German, but in-browser translation ought to work well) explains a GenAI[^genai] R&D 
project conducted by Maria Matache, Luca Zaczkowsky, and Adrian Meister that 
developed such a solution. 

In the process, they set out to address three specific goals (quotes stem from 
the [article][post]):

- **Measurable performance and optimisation**: "understand where time and tokens[^tokens] are being used, and make the system measurably faster and more cost-effective"

- **Configurable data assets**: "integrate new data sets as configurations rather than as code"

- **Ease of re-use**: "reuse the same solution for other use cases or a second site without having to rebuild everything from scratch"

![The inner workings of the solution (in German) (source: EBP)](chatbot-workings.png "The inner workings of the solution (in German) (source: EBP)")

In addition to the goals above, the [article][post] briefly explains guardrails 
to catch off-topic interactions and problematic content, to prohibit mass 
querying, and to cap maximum possible operation costs. Two examples  show the 
behaviour of the working solution in the contexts of the city of Schaffhausen 
and the canton of Zurich.

[![Example "Talk to the map" chat (source: EBP)](geochat-zurich.png "Example 'Talk to the map' chat (source: EBP)")][post]

[^genai]: "Generative AI", that is artificial intelligence systems that generate new media (text, code, images, audio, video) rather than only analysing or classifying existing data.

[^tokens]: The units of text (words or word fragments) that language models process; usage and cost of LLM-based systems are typically measured in tokens.

[^transp]: Transparency note: I work at EBP. I was not involved in the project at hand, however.

[post]: https://digital.ebp.ch/2026/11/02/talk-to-the-map-wie-ein-sprachmodell-gis-daten-zum-reden-bringt/
